plan.planning_summary: Refinement of route_03 (Si/Al2O3 22-layer dual-cavity filter) following iteration_15 completion with best_target_score=0.854. Three complementary routes implement feedback directive to constrain band-edge layer bounds [450,620]nm while exploring material alternatives and layer count variations. All routes maintain parent_route_id=route_03 per refinement_chain requirement.

routes.title: Si/Al2O3 Dual-Cavity Filter with Band-Edge Constrained Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining band-edge layer thickness bounds to [450,620]nm while initializing from previous best candidate with ±4% perturbation will improve spectral transition sharpness and increase best_target_score by redirecting optimization budget from interior phase-trimming to edge sharpening.
routes.design_principle: Dual-cavity defect filter with quarter-wave stack mirrors; band-edge layers control passband transitions while interior layers provide bulk phase matching.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Si/Al2O3]×11 | CaF2 substrate; 22 finite layers total with dual-cavity defect structure: Mirror1(5 pairs)-Cavity1-Mirror2(4 pairs)-Cavity2-Mirror3(5 pairs)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with differentiated bounds: layers 0-3 and 18-21 bounded [450,620]nm, layers 4-17 bounded [400,1100]nm
manufacturing_considerations: Si and Al2O3 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Band-edge layer bounds reflect manufacturable tolerance window
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave stack principle for high-reflectance mirrors
Defect cavity resonance for narrow passband transmission
expected_advantages: Narrower band-edge bounds focus optimization on transition regions
Initialization from previous best candidate reduces search space
±4% perturbation maintains exploration while respecting prior convergence
known_risks: Over-constraining band-edge layers may limit achievable transition sharpness
Local optimum from previous iteration may persist
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate with air incidence at normal incidence. Layer sequence: Si(511nm)/Al2O3(575nm)/Si(576nm)/Al2O3(591nm)/Si(514nm)/Al2O3(578nm)/Si(682nm)/Al2O3(432nm)/Si(493nm)/Al2O3(550nm)/Si(767nm)/Al2O3(452nm)/Si(449nm)/Al2O3(506nm)/Si(792nm)/Al2O3(463nm)/Si(503nm)/Al2O3(1069nm)/Si(737nm)/Al2O3(758nm)/Si(491nm)/Al2O3(655nm). Apply thickness bounds: layers 0-3 and 18-21 bounded [450,620]nm; layers 4-17 bounded [400,1100]nm. Initialize optimization from thickness vector [502.2,538.4,621.0,599.4,496.3,583.2,611.8,497.1,535.4,545.4,906.3,626.7,613.3,510.4,544.6,606.4,629.1,1016.8,461.4,449.6,575.7,865.4]nm with ±4% Gaussian perturbation. Optimize for mean transmittance in 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm bands (maximize) and mean transmittance in 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm bands (minimize). Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to constrain band-edge layer bounds [450,620]nm and initialize from previous best candidate with ±4% perturbation to focus optimization on spectral transition regions.

routes.title: Ge/YbF3 Dual-Cavity Filter with Higher Index Contrast
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Ge/YbF3 material pair provides higher refractive index contrast than Si/Al2O3, enabling sharper spectral transitions and improved stopband blocking with same 22-layer count, potentially increasing best_target_score.
routes.design_principle: Dual-cavity defect filter leveraging high index contrast (Ge n~4.0, YbF3 n~1.5) for steeper band edges with fewer layers required per mirror section.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/YbF3]×11 | CaF2 substrate; 22 finite layers total with dual-cavity defect structure: Mirror1(5 pairs)-Cavity1-Mirror2(4 pairs)-Cavity2-Mirror3(5 pairs)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with quarter-wave initialization at 3300nm and 4250nm center wavelengths
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and YbF3 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Ge requires careful deposition control due to high absorption coefficient
theory_basis: Higher index contrast yields wider stopband and steeper transitions per quarter-wave stack theory
Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Defect cavity resonance for dual-band transmission
expected_advantages: Higher index contrast may achieve equivalent blocking with fewer layers
Steeper band edges improve stopband suppression
Material pair validated in prior IR gas sensor literature
known_risks: Ge absorption may reduce passband transmission
Previous route_03 iteration with Ge/YbF3 failed on material_data - must verify registry availability
Thermal stress mismatch between Ge and YbF3
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate with air incidence at normal incidence. Layer sequence: Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(412nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm)/Ge(206nm)/YbF3(550nm). Apply uniform thickness bounds [300,900]nm to all layers. Initialize optimization from quarter-wave thicknesses at 3300nm center wavelength. Optimize for mean transmittance in 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm bands (maximize) and mean transmittance in 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm bands (minimize). Use differential evolution thickness optimizer with population size 50. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Explores higher index contrast material pair (Ge/YbF3 vs Si/Al2O3) to test whether increased contrast improves stopband blocking and transition sharpness within same 22-layer topology.

routes.title: Si/Al2O3 24-Layer Dual-Cavity Filter with Extended Mirrors
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 22 to 24 by adding one pair to each outer mirror section will improve stopband blocking without degrading passband transmission, increasing best_target_score within the 24-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.design_principle: Dual-cavity defect filter with extended mirror sections (6 pairs outer, 4 pairs inner) to enhance out-of-band rejection while maintaining dual-band transmission.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Si/Al2O3]×12 | CaF2 substrate; 24 finite layers total with dual-cavity defect structure: Mirror1(6 pairs)-Cavity1-Mirror2(4 pairs)-Cavity2-Mirror3(6 pairs)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with quarter-wave initialization; all 24 layers optimizable
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count 24 at maximum allowed constraint
Si and Al2O3 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Additional 2 layers increase deposition time but remain within practical limits
theory_basis: More layers produce steeper spectral slopes and higher out-of-band blocking per interference filter theory
Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with layer pair count
Defect cavity transmission maintained with proper mirror symmetry
expected_advantages: Improved stopband suppression from extended mirrors
Maintained passband transmission with proper cavity design
Uses full 24-layer budget for maximum performance
known_risks: Increased layer count may introduce more spectral ripple in passbands
Longer deposition time increases manufacturing cost
May not provide significant improvement over 22-layer if 22 already near optimum
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate with air incidence at normal incidence. Layer sequence: Si(511nm)/Al2O3(575nm)/Si(576nm)/Al2O3(591nm)/Si(514nm)/Al2O3(578nm)/Si(550nm)/Al2O3(550nm)/Si(682nm)/Al2O3(432nm)/Si(493nm)/Al2O3(550nm)/Si(767nm)/Al2O3(452nm)/Si(449nm)/Al2O3(506nm)/Si(792nm)/Al2O3(463nm)/Si(503nm)/Al2O3(1069nm)/Si(737nm)/Al2O3(758nm)/Si(491nm)/Al2O3(655nm). Apply uniform thickness bounds [400,1100]nm to all 24 layers. Initialize optimization from quarter-wave thicknesses at 3300nm and 4250nm center wavelengths. Optimize for mean transmittance in 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm bands (maximize) and mean transmittance in 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm bands (minimize). Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with learning rate 0.01. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Explores maximum allowed layer count (24 vs 22) to test whether additional mirror pairs improve stopband blocking within manufacturing constraint.
